The hook reads this owner record but **never writes it** — only the run's own agents (the orchestrator and its dispatched build subagents) write it, and only via `faff heartbeat`, which writes the heartbeat sidecar, never the owner block (the close at exit is `faff run close`'s one locked edit). Liveness is on-disk owner-emitted state, never a tracker read, network call, or foreign-pid probe (the pure-function CLI invariant).

### Stop hook (harness-enforced backstop)

Step 11 is agent-run, so it shares the failure mode it guards against — a non-compliant run could skip it. The Stop hook closes that gap: it runs `runcheck --hook` outside the agent's control when the session ends and blocks Stop with a reason if the latest run left admitted issues undispatched. `faff run open` registers faff's Stop-hook command set through `hooks-ensure` (never hand-edit `settings.json`): idempotent and non-destructive, it ensures `runcheck --hook` and `prepcheck --hook` (faff-prep's same-turn-attach guard), and skips any command the resolved `faff` can't serve. In `--hook` mode runcheck stays silent for any session without an open beep-boop ledger. Tell the user when the hook set is added and why (the `hooks-ensure:` stderr line).

**Ownership + liveness gate.** The Stop hook is registered globally and fires on **every** session's turn-end, so a parallel beep-boop drain's legitimately in-flight ledger (admitted, no terminal outcome *yet*) used to false-block an unrelated interactive session. `runcheck --hook` now gates before auditing: it **hard-blocks** only when the resolved run is one **this session owns** (the `FAFF_RUN_DIR` / `FAFF_SESSION_ID` match against the `owner` stamp above — the backstop is preserved for the owning session) **or** a human passes explicit **`--recover`**. A foreign run a live owner is still holding (running + fresh heartbeat) → the hook stays **silent**. A foreign, **not-held** run — `owner` absent (legacy ledger), `status:"done"`, or the **effective heartbeat** (the newer, by parsed epoch, of the heartbeat sidecar and `owner.last_heartbeat` — `overlayHeartbeat`/`effectiveHeartbeatIso`; `runcheck --hook` overlays the sidecar before this check) staler than `FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS` — with undispatched work now **WARNs, never blocks**: still surfaced, never silently dropped, but a non-owning session is never trapped by another run's incompleteness. This is why the owner stamp + lifecycle heartbeat above are load-bearing: they are the on-disk signal that lets the hook tell owned from foreign, and held from abandoned. A legacy ledger with no `owner` is treated as unowned and **warned, not blocked** — the earlier hard block on this path is gone.

## Run-event log (observability substrate)

Append meaningful transitions to `.faff/runs/<run-id>/events.jsonl` using `echo '<payload>' | faff events append --run <run-id>`. Supply only `{phase, type, issue?, data?}`; the CLI owns `schema`, `run_id`, `seq` and `ts`. `seq` orders the timeline; never sort by `ts`. The append-only log is lock-serialised across the orchestrator, `contain --record`, lights-out and detached sentry poller. Emit even under `logging: essential`, but never per-file, test or CI-poll micro-actions. This section produces events for wtf, morning reports and L4 consumers; it does not render them.

Use `faff events validate` to check lines and `faff events read --run <run-id> [--type T] [--issue I]` to read. Each type's permitted `data` keys are in `verification/evidence/v0.3/schema/events/<type>.schema.json`; extra keys are dropped with a warning and named in `data.dropped_keys`.

The mint atomically creates `run-start` with the directory and ledger (`init-self-drain`, or `mintLightsOut` at L4). Never emit a separate genesis row; the table includes it only to show the complete inventory.

| Transition | `phase` / `type` | `--tokens`? |
|---|---|---|
| Run start | `run` / `run-start` | no (delta ~0; seeds the baseline) |
| Tidy pass returns (step 1) | `tidy` / `tidy-done` | **yes** |
| Issue admitted to the build queue (step 4) | `run` / `issue-admitted` (issue) | no |
| Prep of an issue start/finish (step 3) | `prep` / `prep-start` · `prep-done` (issue) | done: **yes**; start: no |
| Graft subagent dispatched (step 6) | `build` / `build-start` (issue) | no |
| Graft subagent returns its token | `build` / `issue-outcome` (issue, `data.outcome`, + `data.gate`/`data.rework_turns` on a non-clean build) | **yes** |
| Discovered-scope ticket filed (steps 7 / 8.0 / 10 — the shared filing mechanism) | `run` / `discovered-scope-filed` | no |
| Budget checkpoint | `run` / `budget-checkpoint` (`data` = `BudgetState`) | **yes** |
| Sentry checkpoint | `run` / `sentry-checkpoint` (`data` = the `faff sentry check` payload, verbatim) | no |
| An issue is parked | `prep`\|`build` / `park` (issue) | **yes** |
| Orchestrator exit (any path) | `run` / `run-end` | **yes** |

**Token-tagging.** On exactly the phase-closing rows marked **yes**, use `echo '<payload>' | faff events append --run <run-id> --tokens --root "$measure_root" --session-id "$session_id"`. Keep the pinned root/session regardless of cwd. Do not tag phase-opening events. The CLI adds counts-only `data.tokens` (`{input, output, cache_write, cache_read}` since the last checkpoint) and `data.tokens_source`: `transcript` when metered, otherwise `estimate` with `tokens: null`. It advances the ledger checkpoint; no prompt/response payload is stored. These are additive under free-form `data`, with `schema` remaining `1`. Attribute prep to `prep-done`, build/review to `issue-outcome`, tidy to `tidy-done`, and residual orchestration to `budget-checkpoint`/`run-end`, not timestamp windows.
